name: Toughness (Solid White)
verdict: Coupon (Test_02, no anti-aliasing) at 12.4 s, bottom 18 s x 4, 295 layers. Printed well. Vat weight before the print is uncertain, so consumption is not used for calibration.

tests.txt: Bars 5.0-19.8 s, after a first round centred on 9.2 s left a doughy surface. From 8.7 s the bars formed, thickness grew to 0.37 mm at 16.7 s and then stopped. Thin bars curl for a while after washing and flatten again as they dry. 12.4 s (0.30 mm) is the lowest bar with a dry surface and sharp pixels - deeper than the black bottle at the same time.
The coupon at 12.4 s, the exposure from the strips. Printed well.
The same coupon at 0.10 mm, 14 s. It printed fine.

Two 14.5 mm lattice cubes. Washed straight after printing, the lattice stays open. Left standing, even for a few minutes, resin trapped in the smallest openings (0.25-0.5 mm on flat faces) hardens and closes them - the plugs come out shinier than the surface, so they cure after the print, not during it. The black bottle does not do this. Lowering the exposure did not help; 9.2 s is the lowest time that keeps the upright cube straight, at 7.8 s it leans. Hard straight off the printer. Photo: 7.8 s, washed within minutes.
